description: An earth-covered wood pile that smoulders with little air
A stone shaft kiln that burns limestone into quicklime
A clay furnace that roasts copper ore and reduces it with charcoal
A charcoal shaft furnace that reduces iron ore to a spongy bloom
A clay crucible set in the fire to melt and mix metals
A bone-ash dish that soaks up molten litharge and leaves silver
A still with a glass head that boils and condenses what it distils
Leaching vats and a boiling pan for crystallizing salts
A tall charcoal furnace that melts iron into pig iron
Sealed chests of iron bars and charcoal held red-hot for days
A closed clay retort that reduces zinc ore and condenses the metal
A pan to work ore with mercury and a hood to drive the mercury off
A clay retort heated white-hot whose neck dips under water
A furnace whose roof throws the flame down onto the ore; the flue catches fumes
An updraft kiln that fires clay into brick and terracotta
Shallow clay pans where sun and wind dry seawater to salt
A copper pot still over a fire: seawater boils and its steam condenses as pure fresh water; the salt stays in the pot
A sealed oak barrel where yeast turns sugar into alcohol
An open vat where wine sours into vinegar in the air
A beehive furnace whose clay pots melt sand with wood ash
A climbing kiln whose last chamber reaches 1300 °C
A brick beehive oven that bakes coal for two days into coke
Clay crucibles of steel melted in a coke fire with a tall chimney
A retort over a water trough that collects the gas it gives off
Electrodes in a molten salt; powered by Voltaic Piles next to it
A porcelain-lined vat where hot acid dissolves ores
A sealed iron crucible where potassium strips oxygen and chlorine from salts
A room of lead sheet where burning sulfur becomes sulfuric acid
A tilting steel pear lined with firebrick: air blown through molten iron burns out its carbon
A steel pressure vessel where hot lye dissolves the alumina out of bauxite
A carbon-lined steel pot of molten cryolite; current splits the alumina dissolved in it
A slate box with a flowing mercury cathode: brine becomes lye and chlorine
A tall cast-iron tower where ammoniated brine meets carbon dioxide
Trays of vanadium catalyst that turn sulfur dioxide into sulfur trioxide
A compressor and copper heat exchanger that liquefy air and boil it apart by temperature
A prism spectroscope with a Bunsen burner: names the traces in a residue so they can be separated
Lead-lined tanks where current carries copper from crude anodes to pure cathodes
Towers where carbon monoxide carries nickel off as a gas and lays it down pure
A platinum U-tube with fluorite stoppers for electrolysing hydrogen fluoride
Three graphite electrodes strike an arc into the charge: ferroalloys and silicon at 2000 °C and more
A thick steel bomb where nitrogen and hydrogen meet over an iron catalyst at 200 atmospheres
Ammonia and air flash over a red-hot platinum-rhodium gauze and become nitric acid
Stirred tanks where oily bubbles carry sulfide grains up as froth and the rock sinks
A hydrogen furnace where pressed tungsten carbide and cobalt powder bake into solid tips
Rows of dishes for crystallizing salts again and again, with a muffle to ignite them to oxides
A glass bulb where a glowing tungsten wire grows a bar of pure metal from its iodide vapour
A brick-lined shaft where chlorine meets hot ore and coke; titanium tetrachloride boils off
A stainless steel retort under argon where molten magnesium strips the chlorine from titanium
Tall glass columns of resin beads: each rare earth comes off in its own band
A quartz crucible of molten silicon under argon; a turning seed draws up one crystal
A boat of germanium drawn slowly through ring heaters: the impurities ride the molten zone
A belt press of cemented carbide anvils: 50000 atmospheres and 1500 °C
Thousands of porous nickel barriers in a row: uranium hexafluoride gas comes out a little richer in uranium-235 at each
Lead walls and a metre of lead glass: remote hands dissolve spent fuel in nitric acid and part it by solvent
Two hollow copper electrodes between the poles of a great magnet whirl alpha particles into a target
A vacuum tank between the poles of a great magnet: ions of each isotope bend into their own collector pocket
A clean room of diffusion furnaces, photomask steppers and etching baths that builds circuits layer by layer on silicon
A linear accelerator and superconducting separator: heavy ions slam into a spinning target and the rare survivors are caught in a detector
A riveted steel still under a fractionating column: oil boils off cut by cut, light to heavy
A pressure still over a furnace that breaks heavy oil into gasoline and gas; later a platinum reformer
A copper kettle over a brick hearth for rendering fat and boiling soap
A wooden screw press that squeezes oil out of seeds
A pit of bark liquor where hides lie for months to become leather
An iron steam pan that cures rubber with sulfur under pressure
A copper-lined vat over a small fire where pigments are precipitated and dyes made
An iron pot still with a column that cuts coal tar into its oils and leaves pitch
A bolted steel pressure vessel for reactions at 200 °C and 20 atmospheres
An electric melt pot at the top of a tall tower: drops of fertilizer freeze into prills as they fall
A steel tank stirred and blown with sterile air: the only way to grow antibiotics by the tonne
A sterile glass and steel vessel run by a chip: engineered microbes make fuels, plastics and medicines
An electric piston compressor: draws in air and fills Steel Cylinders with it, no Compressor upgrade needed
